clue.text: America's burden?

parts.note: a load that is America's to carry rests upon that country; this piece is the short preposition for resting upon something
America is the United States, shortened to its two initials

explanation.surface: A question about what weighs most heavily on the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the whimsy: 'America's' is read as a description, a load lying ON the US, and the two short words run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a duty or responsibility that someone has to carry.

clue.text: Well done choosing beef!

definitions.meaning: a cry of congratulation, these days usually said with a dry edge
bully is corned beef, once a British army ration, so a diner who picks it is told the tinned meat is theirs

explanation.surface: Someone is congratulated on ordering the beef, perhaps cooked right through.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned cry of congratulation which, taken word by word, hands corned beef to the person addressed.

clue.text: Compensate for not filming

definitions.meaning: to make up for something, to counterbalance it
an actor who is not filming is away from the studio floor where the cameras roll; taken as two three-letter words

explanation.surface: Making amends for a day when the cameras did not roll.
explanation.definitionFit: To counterbalance a loss is one sense; split into two short words it describes an actor away from the studio floor.

clue.text: Panted like a scarlet runner perhaps

definitions.text: Panted like a scarlet runner perhaps

parts.words: Panted like a scarlet runner perhaps
parts.note: a scarlet runner is a climbing bean, but here it is an athlete gone red in the face and gasping after the race; the phrase describes that state

explanation.surface: A climbing bean plant, of all things, is pictured puffing and wheezing.
explanation.walkthrough: A scarlet runner is a red-flowered runner bean, common in British gardens. The clue wants the other runner: one on a track, flushed and gasping.
explanation.definitionFit: A racer who is flushed and gasping for air has no wind left in the lungs.

clue.text: Covered with fine powder — sounds fancy

indicators.note: the clue says the powdery word sounds like a word for fancy, so listen to it rather than spell it

parts.note: fancy in the sense of ornate: flowery language is elaborate and over-decorated

explanation.surface: Something dusted with a fine powder strikes the speaker as rather posh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds' signals a homophone: FLOWERY, said aloud, is the answer. On the surface 'sounds fancy' just means 'seems posh'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything dusted with the baker's ground wheat, such as a kneading board, is coated in fine white powder.

clue.text: The Parisian stood up genuflecting whilst nudging

indicators.note: this is a down entry, so a word that has stood up is written climbing from bottom to top

parts.note: le is 'the' in French, as a Parisian would say it
to genuflect is to bend the knee in reverence, loosely to bow

explanation.surface: A man from Paris got to his feet, bent the knee and jostled his neighbour all at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stood up' turns LE into EL, a reversal that works because this is a down clue. 'whilst' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: jostling or prodding someone with the bent joint of the arm.

clue.text: Frenchman and I lead the way despite the haze

indicators.note: lead says the Frenchman and I go in front of the piece for the way

parts.note: M is the abbreviation of Monsieur, the title of a Frenchman
taken as written
a way is a street, abbreviated St in addresses

explanation.surface: A Frenchman and the speaker walk at the front of the party even though visibility is poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' puts M and I ahead of ST. 'despite the' is only a join to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: thin fog, a veil of fine droplets that blurs the view.

clue.text: Amount of cash turned over, one thousand pounds for background music

indicators.note: this is a down entry, so a word turned over is flipped to read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money
one can be the article a, as in 'a thousand'
K is informal for a thousand, especially of money: a salary of 40K

explanation.surface: A firm's takings of a thousand pounds all came from piped background music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' reads SUM upwards as MUS. It looks like business turnover, which is why the cash is there.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the piped recorded tunes played in lifts, shops and waiting rooms, from the trade name of the firm that supplied them.

clue.text: Man wrong about Missouri

indicators.note: about means the word for a wrong goes around the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: a wrong, as a noun, is a sin
MO is the US postal abbreviation for Missouri

explanation.surface: A fellow holds a mistaken belief concerning the state of Missouri.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reads as 'concerning' on the surface; here it is the wrapping signal. A bare 'Man' for a forename is as vague as definitions come, so the wordplay has to do the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a male forename, borne by the apostle Peter before he was renamed.

clue.text: Gold inside damaged urn on Pacific island

indicators.note: inside says the gold goes within the letters made from the urn
a damaged urn is broken up, so its three letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Au is the chemical symbol for gold, from the Latin aurum

explanation.surface: Treasure is discovered within a broken vase on a South Sea isle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' reorders the vase's three letters to NRU, and 'inside' then sets the chemical symbol after the N. 'on' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a tiny republic in Micronesia, one of the world's smallest states.

clue.text: Bother few who are upsetting

parts.note: bother, as noun or verb, is trouble
a few is some: a small number

explanation.surface: An order to pester the handful of people who are causing distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' looks like an instruction to disturb the earlier words, but it is the definition; 'who are' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym, near enough: a thing that causes worry and vexation distresses whoever must deal with it.

clue.text: Most of ointment, round used for discharge

indicators.note: most of tells you to use the word for ointment without its final letter

parts.note: a salve is a soothing ointment
the letter O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Nearly all the ointment, applied in a circle, went on treating a weeping wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' trims SALVE to SALV. The discharge is not medical: it is a volley of gunfire; 'used for' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the military sense: a volley of guns all fired together.

clue.text: One doesn't get cold feet in this ceremony

definitions.text: One doesn't get cold feet in this ceremony

parts.words: One doesn't get cold feet in this ceremony
parts.note: cold feet usually means a loss of nerve; here it is literal, since the ritual has people step barefoot across hot embers

explanation.surface: Nobody loses their nerve and backs out of this particular ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: In this ritual people cross a bed of glowing embers barefoot, so their soles are anything but chilly.

clue.text: Nimble, certainly not heavy-handed

definitions.meaning: quick and graceful in movement, treading delicately
a playful opposite built piece by piece: swap heavy for its antonym, and swap hands for the other extremities

explanation.surface: Someone deft is described as having nothing clumsy or overbearing about them.
explanation.definitionFit: An agile person treads delicately, and the phrase is also the piece-by-piece opposite of a clumsy, overbearing touch.

clue.text: During tense time to come

definitions.note: a noun phrase where the answer is adverbial; the fuller idiom 'in time to come' is the exact match

parts.note: during a period means in it: during the war, in the war
the future is a grammatical tense, alongside the past and the present

explanation.surface: Throughout the nerve-racking period that lies ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' reads as 'nervous' but is the grammar term, here THE FUTURE. The definition is loose: it needs 'in' in front to substitute cleanly.
explanation.definitionFit: Loosely: what lies ahead is the time to come, and the idiom 'in time to come' gives the adverbial sense.

clue.text: Appliance that had been tagged wrongly

indicators.note: something tagged wrongly is out of order, so the letters of that word are put in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A piece of household kit had been given the wrong label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges TAGGED; 'that had been' only joins it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Near-synonym: both are devices made for a particular job, though this word suggests something smaller and cleverer.

clue.text: Describe word grammatically concerning astronomical distance

parts.note: to parse a word is to state its part of speech and its role in the sentence
concerning means about, and about is also circa, abbreviated c

explanation.surface: A grammar exercise on a term that has to do with distances in space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concerning' gives C in two steps: concerning is 'about', and 'about' with dates is circa, written c.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a unit of length for the gaps between stars, about 3.26 light years.

clue.text: A pig died on the ship

parts.note: taken as written
a boar is a male pig
d is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees

explanation.surface: An animal carried as livestock perished during the voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: on or onto a vessel, where passengers and crew are.

clue.text: Dubbed king Edward about the end of the day

indicators.note: about puts the king and Edward around the word for the end of the day

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess and cards
Ed is the short form of Edward
night is what comes when the day ends

explanation.surface: Someone was nicknamed King Edward towards nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the wrapping signal: the king and Edward stand either side of the day's end. 'Dubbed' reads as 'nicknamed'; here it is the tap of a sword that makes someone a Sir.
explanation.definitionFit: To dub someone is to tap their shoulder with a sword and confer the title Sir.

clue.text: Beg or borrow perhaps, not his grouchiness developing

indicators.note: developing suggests the letters left over change and grow into a new shape, so they are rearranged
not his tells you those three letters are left out of the longer word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cadging from people is to blame, rather than his bad temper getting worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes H, I and S out of GROUCHINESS, leaving GROUCNES for 'developing' to rearrange. 'Beg or borrow' echoes the saying 'beg, borrow or steal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: to cadge something off others covers both asking for it and taking it on loan, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Thus unknown origin said to be for salty dark brown liquid

parts.note: thus means so: in this way
in algebra an unknown quantity is written x, y or z; here it is y

indicators.note: said tells you the word for origin is spoken, and a like-sounding word is what gets written

parts.note: the source of something is its origin

explanation.surface: Someone explains that a salty brown fluid is of mysterious provenance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' signals a homophone: SOURCE sounds like SAUCE in most English accents, where the r is silent. 'to be for' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the fermented bean condiment of Chinese and Japanese cooking, thin, very salty and nearly black.

clue.text: First two vowels for goddess

parts.note: the first vowel of the alphabet
the pair come in order, one and afterwards the other; this piece is the word for afterwards or next
the second vowel of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A deity is awarded the opening pair of vowels.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is spelt out as a sequence: of the vowels A, E, I, O, U, the first is followed by the second, and the word for 'followed by' sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Greek deity of wisdom and warfare, patron of the city named after her.

clue.text: Invent what to do after quarrel

definitions.meaning: to concoct or fabricate, as with a story or an excuse
after a row the thing to do is be reconciled and become friends again

explanation.surface: Dream up something to do once the argument is over.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to concoct something, such as an excuse, and to become reconciled after a row.

clue.text: Lazy person's seat next to Murphy

indicators.note: next to places the seat directly beside the word for Murphy

parts.note: a couch is a long upholstered seat, a sofa
a murphy is informal, originally Irish, slang for a potato

explanation.surface: An idler's chair is the one beside a man named Murphy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay. Murphy is no surname here: it is old slang for a potato, from Ireland's link with the crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone who lounges in front of the television all day instead of being active.

clue.text: Beast to get up before second half of winter

indicators.note: before puts the upturned word ahead of the letters taken from winter
this is a down entry, so a word told to get up is written climbing from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: second half of takes the last three of winter's six letters

explanation.surface: An animal must rouse itself from sleep before midwinter has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get up' is a reversal signal only because this is a down entry: the two-letter word climbs the grid, giving OT. 'second half of' halves winter and 'before' fixes the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a river-dwelling, fish-eating mammal of the weasel family.

clue.text: Incomplete mark of authenticity for hidden store

indicators.note: incomplete says the word for a mark of authenticity is missing its final letter

parts.note: a cachet is an official seal or stamp vouching that something is genuine

explanation.surface: Only a partial hallmark vouches for a secret stockpile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incomplete' drops the last letter of CACHET, leaving the answer; 'for' joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a secret stockpile of food, arms or treasure, tucked away for later.

clue.text: In the shop tediously made a selection

indicators.note: In says the answer sits inside the run of letters that the following words make

explanation.surface: A customer took a boringly long time to choose something in the store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals that the answer is spelt out across the join of 'shop' and 'tediously'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: chose one thing from several, as in having plumped for the cheaper model.

clue.text: Inactive queen of Carthage?

parts.note: someone inactive performed nothing at all; this piece is the past-tense verb for performed
what the inactive person achieved was nothing, written as a zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A question about a Carthaginian ruler who sat idle.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the whimsy: someone inactive DID nothing, and nothing is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in Virgil's Aeneid she is the founder and ruler of Carthage who falls for Aeneas.

clue.text: Creature to remain with group

parts.note: to stick is to stay put, as in sticking with a plan
someone with a group is in it, one of its members
a sect is a group, usually a religious one that has broken away

explanation.surface: An animal that prefers to stay with its herd.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a long, thin bug that hides by looking like a twig of the plant it sits on.

clue.text: German man did not start limited edition as he had gone wrong

indicators.note: did not start means the German word loses its opening letter

parts.note: Herr is German for Mr, the title of a German man
ed is the standard short form of edition; limited here means cut short

explanation.surface: A German failed to begin a collector's print run because he had made a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'did not start' takes the H off HERR. A limited edition is normally a small print run; here 'limited' means abbreviated. 'as he had' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: having made a mistake or strayed from the right course.

clue.text: One doesn't have to count the cost of such items

definitions.text: One doesn't have to count the cost of such items

parts.words: One doesn't have to count the cost of such items
parts.note: counting the cost usually means weighing up the consequences; taken literally, nothing needs adding up when each item's price is zero

explanation.surface: There is no need to fret over the consequences of these things.
explanation.definitionFit: Items given away for nothing carry no price, so there is no bill to add up.

clue.text: It is essential that launching area has push-button controls

definitions.note: plural in the clue though the answer is one device: a single panel carries all the buttons

parts.note: key, as an adjective, means essential or crucial
a pad is the platform a rocket is launched from

explanation.surface: A rule for a rocket base: the launch site must be worked by push-buttons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It is', 'that' and 'has' only hold the sentence together; the answer is one device, defined a little loosely by a plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small panel of buttons, as on a phone or a cash machine, used to operate a device.
